messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Canary healthcheck degraded for customer veridian (veridian-vpc).
impacted pool: veridian-pool-3
symptom: 5xx rate spike from 3.2% -> 7.9% over 5m, p50 latency +45% (grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/veridian/canary)

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started by @maria at 2026-03-12T09:11:23Z. artifact: sha256:abcd1234efgh5678. traffic=10% -> hosts: pool-3

henry: paging SRE oncall -> @ryan :eyes:  this is the canary from the 09:11 deploy, saw the alert. can you take initial triage?

ryan: ack. pulling logs now, grabbing pod/container ids.

ashley: quick note — in the container logs I'm seeing repeated KV cache miss floods then GC OOM logs on gateway process on node g4dn-16-03. stack traces point at kv-cache refresh path.

maria: veridian support pinged us ~09:18, they see 502s in their dashboard for model veridian-llm-beta. customer impact: some inference requests failing (~3-4% of traffic currently routed to canary).

henry: TL;DR mitigation plan: 1) isolate affected tenant traffic if we can 2) pause canary rollout / pin pool back to previous artifact 3) divert remaining veridian traffic to fallback reserved pool (veridian-pool-fallback) 4) collect logs + postmortem.

ashley: runbook reference: https://internal/runbooks/canary-failure (see section "tenant isolation + rollback").

ryan: running orchestrator pause ->
```
curl -X POST https://orch.internal/api/v1/deploys/pause -d '{"pool":"veridian-pool-3","reason":"canary 5xx spike"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

deploy-bot: Orchestrator accepted pause request for pool veridian-pool-3. status=PAUSED. traffic-statement: canary traffic stopped for rollout id r-20260312-0911

ashley: confirming current artifact on pool-3 = sha256:abcd1234efgh5678. previous known-good artifact = sha256:zzzz9999yyyy8888.

henry: instructing ops to pin pool -> set pinned_sha to zzzz9999yyyy8888 and trigger immediate pinback. @deploy-bot can you run the pin command or give me the curl snippet?

deploy-bot: pin command:
```
curl -X POST https://orch.internal/api/v1/pools/pin -d '{"pool":"veridian-pool-3","pinned_sha":"sha256:zzzz9999yyyy8888","reason":"emergency canary revert"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

ryan: executing pin now.

ryan: pin acknowledged by orchestrator. applying pinned artifact to pool - rolling hosts to pinned image with zero-downtime preference.

ashley: while rolling, I'm isolating tenant routing for veridian to avoid partial traffic hitting the bad canary: updating routing rule ->
```
POST /routing/update
{ "tenant": "veridian", "route_to": "veridian-pool-fallback", "force": true }
```

deploy-bot: routing update accepted. veridian traffic rerouted to veridian-pool-fallback. note: fallback pool is on older artifact sha256:zzzz9999yyyy8888.

maria: messaged customer: "We observed increased errors from today's canary. We've paused the rollout and routed you to a verified pool. You may see transient failures while we complete the rollback. We'll follow up once everything is stable." :white_check_mark:

ryan: metrics: error rate for veridian dropped from 7.9% -> 1.1% within 90s after reroute. p50 lat returning to baseline.

ashley: logs show the OOM and cache miss storm subsided after pinback; no node restarts observed during pinback. collecting detailed logs to S3: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2087654321/

henry: great. notifying PD to update on-call handoff: @pagerduty this is now contained, handing ownership to henry for postmortem + customer comms.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged. On-call handover: ryan -> henry. New assignee: henry. severity downgraded to sev-2 (customer impact contained).

maria: customer confirmation: "Service restored, thanks. We'll look out and confirm for an hour." they asked for root cause and timeline.

henry: action items: - create incident ticket (INC-2087654321) - collect config diff and artifact hashes - run bisect on canary artifact in staging - schedule postmortem meeting with veridian + eng-ml (tomorrow 10:00 PT)

ashley: preliminary hypothesis: cache refresh change in new artifact (sha256:abcd1234efgh5678) introduced a pathological prefix eviction pattern under veridian's traffic distribution causing cache storms and memory pressure. will reproduce in CI.

ryan: tagging logs, traces, and sample requests in ticket. also adding reconciliation steps for orchestration API.

henry: marking this thread as resolved once postmortem created. leaving a note to include clearer presubmit perf tests for cache refresh.

incident-bot: Incident resolved. summary: canary rollout paused and pinned back to previous artifact; routing snapback to fallback pool. customer impact: transient 502s affecting ~3-4% of Veridian requests, contained within ~5 minutes. follow-up: postmortem + customer sync scheduled.

maria: thanks all. :heart: good quick work. will draft customer-facing postmortem and send to legal/AM for review.

henry: closing loop. if any additional regressions surface reopen INC-2087654321 or ping #incidents.

deploy-bot: artifact pin event logged: pool=veridian-pool-3 pinned_from=sha256:abcd1234efgh5678 pinned_to=sha256:zzzz9999yyyy8888 by=ryan at=2026-03-12T09:19:48Z.

henry: end of thread. "postmortem required" label: true.
